item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 060536
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sat Sep 5 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Lowell, located about 600 miles south-southwest of the Hawaiian
Islands, on Tropical Storm Karina, located about 750 miles
east-northeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Marie,
located several hundred miles west of the southern tip of the
Baja California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
A trough of low pressure located several hundred miles south of the
coast of southwestern Mexico is producing disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Gradual development of this system is possible, and a
tropical depression could form during the middle or latter portions
of next week while the system moves generally west-northwestward at
10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Marie Public Advisory Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 060847
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Marie Advisory Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026
 
...MARIE FORECAST TO BEGIN WEAKENING LATER TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...23.1N 121.9W
ABOUT 765 MI...1225 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...971 MB...28.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located
near latitude 23.1 North, longitude 121.9 West. Marie is moving
toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h) and this motion is 
expected to continue through today. A turn toward the west- 
northwest is forecast tonight or on Monday. Marie is then expected 
to resume a northwestward heading at a faster forward speed by 
Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Steady weakening is expected to begin later today and 
continue for the next several days. Marie is forecast to become a 
post-tropical remnant low on Wednesday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 50 miles (85 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles
(295 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 971 mb (28.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of
the coast of southwest Mexico, the Baja California Peninsula, and
Southern California for the next few days. These swells are likely
to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip
current risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026 
850 
WTPZ43 KNHC 060847
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026

Convection associated with Marie, while showing well organized 
banding,  has diminished some in intensity since the last advisory. 
However, this has not yet translated into a notable weakening in the 
various satellite intensity estimates. Thus, the initial intensity 
remains a possibly generous 80 kt.

The initial motion is 315/7 kt. Marie is currently being steered by 
a mid- to upper-level ridge to the northeast and heading for a 
break in the ridge caused by a large trough over the U. S. West 
Coast. This trough is forecast to move northeastward during the 
next 24 h, allowing some ridging to develop north of Marie and turn 
the cyclone west-northwestward. By 48 h, a new trough developing to 
the northwest of Marie should turn the cyclone back to a northwest 
motion, with the low-level center continuing this general motion 
until the system dissipates.  The new forecast track is in good 
agreement with the HCCA Corrected Consensus, the Google DeepMind 
ensemble mean, and the Florida State Superensemble.

Marie is starting to move into sea surface temperatures below 26C, 
and the the temperatures get progressively colder along the 
forecast track. This, combined with some dry air entrainment, 
should start a steady weakening later today.  After 48 h, 
increasing shear should cause the cyclone to become decoupled 
vertically, which should lead to the convection dissipating and the 
cyclone becoming post-tropical between 72-96 h. The global models 
forecast the low-level circulation to dissipate completely by 120 h, 
and the intensity forecast follows this.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

120H  11/0600Z...DISSIPATED
